sections.content: How many people are "nursery education teaching professionals"?

15,090 people

were counted on the census as "nursery education teaching professionals" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Nursery education teaching professionals care for and teach children up to the age of entry into primary school.

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "nursery education teaching professionals" there were more women than men (94.5% compared with 5.5%).

This means "nursery education teaching professionals" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "teaching and other educational professionals".

Men made up 5.5% and women made up 94.5% of "nursery education teaching professionals"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "nursery education teaching professionals" included:

  • personal assistants and other secretaries
  • registered community nurses
  • medical secretaries

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 30 to 34 years. Of the whole working population 12% were aged 30 to 34 years. For people working as "nursery education teaching professionals", 15% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "nursery education teaching professionals" was 16 to 19 years.

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "nursery education teaching professionals", 8.1% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (64.8% compared with 35.2%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (95.3%) than self-employed (4.7%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Wandsworth, this is in the same region of London.
